```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(knitr)
  library(yaml)
})
root <- normalizePath("..")
f   <- function(...) file.path(root, ...)
img <- function(path, width = "85%") knitr::include_graphics(f(path))
rd  <- function(path) fread(f(path))
metric <- function(tab, m) tab[metric == m, value]
pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(round(100 * x, d), "%")
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
short <- function(x) gsub("_", " ", sub("^(HALLMARK|REACTOME)_", "", x))

prov   <- yaml::read_yaml(f("data/processed/download_provenance.yaml"))
sheet  <- rd("data/processed/sample_sheet_paired.tsv")
flags  <- rd("results/qc/qc_sample_flags.tsv")
de_all <- rd("results/de/deseq2_all_genes.tsv")
de_sig <- rd("results/de/deseq2_significant.tsv")
sens   <- rd("results/de/sensitivity_summary.tsv")
pur    <- rd("results/de/purity_check.tsv")
hall   <- rd("results/gsea/fgsea_hallmark.tsv")
reac   <- rd("results/gsea/fgsea_reactome.tsv")
conc   <- rd("results/gsea/hallmark_gsea_vs_ora.tsv")
val    <- rd("results/validation/validation_summary.tsv")
anc    <- rd("results/ancestry/ancestry_summary.tsv")
race_h <- rd("results/ancestry/tcga_race_hallmark.tsv")
site_h <- rd("results/ancestry/tcga_race_site_matched_hallmark.tsv")
mt     <- rd("results/ancestry/tcga_race_mt_pseudogene_hits.tsv")
geo_ph <- rd("results/ancestry/geo_ancestry_hallmark_pairlevel.tsv")
race_s <- rd("results/ancestry/tcga_race_sample_sheet.tsv")
hi_grade <- race_s[, .(p = mean(gleason_group == "GS8_10")), by = race]
hg <- function(r) pct(hi_grade[race == r, p])
n_black_pairs <- if ("race" %in% names(sheet))
  sum(sheet[condition == "tumor"]$race == "black or african american", na.rm = TRUE) else NA

n_pairs <- uniqueN(sheet$patient)
n_up    <- sum(de_sig$direction == "up"); n_down <- sum(de_sig$direction == "down")
h_sig   <- hall[padj < 0.05]
n_flag  <- sum(flags$flagged)

# M8: composition and progression
dcs    <- rd("results/deconv/deconv_summary.tsv")
dc_pt  <- rd("results/deconv/paired_composition_tests.tsv")
dc_ah  <- rd("results/deconv/adjusted_paired_hallmark.tsv")
dc_rc  <- rd("results/deconv/race_composition.tsv")
dc_ra  <- rd("results/deconv/race_adjusted_hallmark.tsv")
svs    <- rd("results/survival/survival_summary.tsv")
cox    <- rd("results/survival/cox_results.tsv")
mval   <- function(tab, m) { v <- tab[metric == m, value]; suppressWarnings(if (!is.na(as.numeric(v))) as.numeric(v) else v) }
ifn_a  <- dc_ra[pathway == "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE"]
ifn_g  <- dc_ra[pathway == "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"]
sig_up <- function(nes, padj) isTRUE(padj < 0.05 & nes > 0)
ifn_est <- sig_up(ifn_g$NES_est, ifn_g$padj_est) || sig_up(ifn_a$NES_est, ifn_a$padj_est)
ifn_mcp <- sig_up(ifn_g$NES_mcp, ifn_g$padj_mcp) || sig_up(ifn_a$NES_mcp, ifn_a$padj_mcp)
ifn_text <- if (ifn_est && ifn_mcp) {
  "survives adjustment for immune and stromal content by both methods"
} else if (ifn_mcp) {
  "survives adjustment for lineage-based T-cell, B-cell and fibroblast scores (MCP-counter) but not for ESTIMATE scores, whose immune signature shares genes with the interferon sets"
} else if (ifn_est) {
  "survives the ESTIMATE adjustment but not adjustment for T-cell, B-cell and fibroblast content (MCP-counter)"
} else {
  "does not survive adjustment for immune and stromal content by either method, so it cannot be separated from differences in immune-cell content"
}
core   <- dc_ah[class == "robust to composition" & class_full == "robust to composition"][order(-NES_main)]
cox_adj <- cox[model == "adjusted"][order(p)]
cox_uni <- cox[model == "univariable"][order(p)]
n_cox_sig <- sum(cox_adj$padj < 0.05)
uni_sig <- cox_uni[padj < 0.05]
best_gain <- cox_adj[which.max(c_gain_vs_clinical)]
hr_txt <- function(d) paste0(d$score, " (HR ", round(d$HR_per_SD, 2), " per SD, adjusted p = ", signif(d$padj, 2), ")", collapse = "; ")

# M9: genetic ancestry
gas    <- rd("results/genetic_ancestry/genetic_ancestry_summary.tsv")
ga_sh  <- rd("results/genetic_ancestry/ancestry_sample_sheet.tsv")
ga_hh  <- rd("results/genetic_ancestry/afr_hallmark.tsv")
ga_gt  <- rd("results/genetic_ancestry/germline_gene_tests.tsv")
ga_ifn <- rd("results/genetic_ancestry/ifn_vs_afr.tsv")
gv     <- function(m) { v <- gas[metric == m, value]; n <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v)); if (length(n) && !is.na(n)) n else v }
germ   <- ga_gt[likely_germline == TRUE]
ifng_afr <- ga_hh[pathway == "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"]
ifn_afr_sig <- isTRUE(ifng_afr$padj_afr < 0.05 & ifng_afr$NES_afr > 0)
ifn_pt_p  <- ga_ifn$p[1]; ifn_pt_b <- ga_ifn$beta_sd_per_full_AFR[1]
ifn_pt_sig <- isTRUE(ifn_pt_p < 0.05 & ifn_pt_b > 0)
```

# Summary {.unnumbered}

- **Paired design.** `r n_pairs` TCGA-PRAD patients with both a primary tumor and adjacent normal sample (`r 2 * n_pairs` libraries; GDC data release `r prov$gdc_data_release`).
- **Differential expression.** `r fmt(nrow(de_sig))` genes differ at FDR < 0.05 and ≥ 2-fold (`r fmt(n_up)` up, `r fmt(n_down)` down in tumor). The top genes are established prostate cancer markers (`r paste(head(de_sig$gene_name, 6), collapse = ", ")`).
- **Pathways.** `r nrow(h_sig)` of 50 Hallmark sets are enriched: MYC targets, proliferation (E2F, G2M) and androgen response up; smooth-muscle, stromal and inflammatory programmes down.
- **Robust to QC choices.** Excluding `r n_flag` borderline-purity tumors leaves fold changes almost unchanged (Spearman ρ = `r sens$spearman_log2FC_all`).
- **Independent validation (GSE104131).** In `r metric(val, "complete_pairs")` high-grade pairs, `r pct(metric(val, "sign_agreement_tcga_DEGs"))` of TCGA DEGs change in the same direction, a TCGA-derived signature separates tumor from normal with AUC = `r metric(val, "signature_auc")`, and `r metric(val, "hallmark_replicated")` of `r nrow(h_sig)` Hallmark sets replicate.
- **Ancestry (exploratory).** In gene-set analyses, tumors from Black patients show higher interferon-α/γ signalling than tumors from White patients, robust to tissue-source-site adjustment and reproduced with genetic ancestry. At the patient level the shift is modest (`r sprintf("%+.2f", ifn_pt_b)` SD per unit African ancestry, p = `r signif(ifn_pt_p, 2)`) and tracks immune-cell content. No ancestry-specific tumor-vs-normal effect was detectable in the small validation cohort.
- **Genetic ancestry.** Using published genetic ancestry proportions instead of self-reported race, Hallmark results correlate at r = `r gv("nes_r_afr_vs_race")` with the race-based analysis. `r if (nrow(germ)) paste0(nrow(germ), " of the ", nrow(ga_gt), " top race-associated genes (", paste(head(germ$gene, 6), collapse = ", "), ") track African-ancestry fraction in a pattern that points to inherited variation") else paste0("None of the ", nrow(ga_gt), " top race-associated genes met the germline criteria")`.
- **Tissue composition.** Tumors contain far less smooth muscle and basal epithelium than matched normal tissue. `r nrow(core)` Hallmark sets stay significant in the same direction under every composition adjustment, the strongest candidates for tumor-cell programmes (`r paste(head(short(core[NES_main > 0]$pathway), 6), collapse = ", ")` among those up). The interferon difference between Black and White patients' tumors `r ifn_text`.
- **Progression.** In `r mval(svs, "cox_complete_cases")` tumors with `r mval(svs, "cox_events")` progression events, `r if (n_cox_sig == 0) paste0("no expression score was associated with progression-free interval once Gleason group, T stage and age were included", if (nrow(uni_sig)) paste0("; before adjustment, ", paste(uni_sig$score, collapse = ", "), " predicted faster progression, a signal already carried by Gleason grade") else "") else paste0(n_cox_sig, " of ", nrow(cox_adj), " expression scores remained associated with progression-free interval after adjusting for Gleason group, T stage and age")`.

# Data and design

| | Discovery | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| Cohort | TCGA-PRAD (GDC) | GEO GSE104131 |
| Samples | `r n_pairs` tumor / matched normal pairs | `r metric(val, "complete_pairs")` pairs (`r metric(val, "pairs_AA")` African-American, `r metric(val, "pairs_EA")` European-American) |
| Tumors | All Gleason grades | High grade (Gleason ≥ 4+3) |
| Counts | GDC STAR counts (GENCODE v36), unstranded | NCBI-generated raw counts (GRCh38.p13) |
| Model | DESeq2, `~ patient + condition` | DESeq2, `~ pair + condition` |

All steps run as a Snakemake pipeline. Pairing keeps one aliquot per patient and sample type. Thresholds throughout: FDR < 0.05; DEG lists additionally require |log~2~FC| ≥ 1 on apeglm-shrunken estimates.

# Quality control

```{r qc-numbers}
qc_genes <- nrow(de_all)
```

Genes were kept if they had ≥ 10 reads in at least `r n_pairs` samples (the size of each group), leaving `r fmt(qc_genes)` genes. After variance-stabilising transformation, the first two principal components separate tumor from normal. Neither tissue source site nor sequencing plate is associated with them, so no batch correction was applied.

```{r fig-pca, fig.cap = "PCA of the 500 most variable genes. Grey lines join each patient's tumor and normal sample."}
img("results/qc/pca_condition.png", "75%")
```

**Tumor purity.** `r n_flag` tumors sat nearer the normal cluster on the PCA. A marker score (tumor-up genes AMACR, PCA3, HPN, DLX1, TDRD1 minus basal-cell genes KRT5, KRT15, TP63, MYLK, CNN1) did not flag them. Published purity estimates, where available, placed them in the lowest quartile (`r paste(na.omit(round(pur[qc_flagged == TRUE]$paper_avgRNA_purity, 2)), collapse = ", ")` vs a median of `r round(median(pur$paper_avgRNA_purity, na.rm = TRUE), 2)` for all paired tumors). All pairs were kept for the main analysis, with a sensitivity analysis excluding them (Section 4.2).

```{r fig-purity, fig.cap = "Marker-based purity check. Lines join pairs; dashed line is the 90th percentile of normals."}
img("results/qc/purity_marker_score.png", "55%")
```

# Differential expression

```{r de-numbers}
n_any <- sum(de_all$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

`r fmt(n_any)` genes differ at FDR < 0.05 (`r pct(n_any / nrow(de_all))` of those tested), which is expected with `r n_pairs` well-matched pairs. Requiring a 2-fold change gives `r fmt(nrow(de_sig))` DEGs. More genes fall than rise in tumors. That fits tumors replacing normal fibromuscular stroma and basal cells.

```{r fig-volcano, fig.cap = "Volcano plot. Fold changes are apeglm-shrunken."}
img("results/de/volcano.png", "80%")
```

```{r tab-top}
top <- head(de_sig[order(padj)], 15)[, .(Gene = gene_name, Type = gene_type,
         `log2FC (shrunk)` = round(log2FC_shrunk, 2), `Adjusted p` = signif(padj, 3))]
kable(top, caption = "Top 15 DEGs by adjusted p-value")
```

The leading genes are among the best-validated prostate cancer markers: AMACR, PCA3, HPN, DLX1 and TDRD1, as well as the prostate-cancer-associated lncRNA PCSEAT. Five of these were also in the QC marker score. That is not circular, because the score was used only to flag samples, never to select them.

```{r fig-heatmap, fig.cap = "Top 50 DEGs (VST, row-centred)."}
img("results/de/top50_heatmap.png", "75%")
```

## Sensitivity to borderline-purity tumors

Refitting without the `r n_flag` flagged pairs (`r sens$pairs_sensitivity` pairs) gives `r fmt(sens$sig_sensitivity)` DEGs versus `r fmt(sens$sig_main)` on matching thresholds. The two lists overlap with Jaccard = `r sens$jaccard`, all overlapping genes change in the same direction, and fold changes correlate at ρ = `r sens$spearman_log2FC_all`.

```{r fig-sens, fig.cap = "Fold changes with and without the flagged pairs."}
img("results/de/sensitivity_concordance.png", "55%")
```

# Pathway analysis

Genes were ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, keeping one Ensembl ID per symbol. fgsea then ran on MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome sets of 15–500 genes. Redundant Reactome pathways were collapsed with `collapsePathways`.

```{r fig-hallmark, fig.cap = "Significant Hallmark sets (labels show adjusted p)."}
img("results/gsea/hallmark_nes.png", "85%")
```

**Up in tumor:** `r paste(short(h_sig[NES > 0][order(-NES)]$pathway), collapse = ", ")`. MYC activation and androgen-receptor signalling are hallmark features of prostate adenocarcinoma, and the proliferation sets reflect a higher mitotic index.

**Down in tumor:** `r paste(short(h_sig[NES < 0][order(NES)]$pathway), collapse = ", ")`. Most of these sets are dominated by smooth-muscle, fibroblast and immune genes. In bulk RNA-seq they largely reflect **tissue composition**: tumors contain less fibromuscular stroma than normal prostate. They are not evidence that tumor cells switch these programmes off. The Hallmark "EMT" set falls for the same reason, because it is mostly stromal genes such as collagens.

```{r fig-reactome, fig.cap = "Top non-redundant Reactome pathways."}
img("results/gsea/reactome_top_dotplot.png", "90%")
```

Of the `r nrow(h_sig)` significant Hallmark sets, `r sum(conc$agrees, na.rm = TRUE)` were also significant by over-representation analysis of the DEG lists. ORA only sees genes past the 2-fold cutoff. Proliferation genes typically move less than 2-fold but move together, so GSEA detects them and ORA misses them.

# Independent validation (GSE104131)

GSE104131 contains 16 high-grade tumor / adjacent-normal pairs (8 African-American, 8 European-American). Four libraries are absent from the NCBI count matrix, leaving `r metric(val, "complete_pairs")` complete pairs.

```{r tab-val}
vt <- data.table(
  Check = c("TCGA DEGs measured in GEO", "Same direction in GEO", "Also FDR < 0.05 in GEO",
            "Fold-change correlation, all shared genes", "TCGA signature AUC (tumor vs normal)",
            "Pairs where tumor scores higher", "Hallmark NES correlation", "Hallmark sets replicated"),
  Result = c(fmt(metric(val, "tcga_DEGs_in_geo")), pct(metric(val, "sign_agreement_tcga_DEGs")),
             fmt(metric(val, "replicated_tcga_DEGs_geo_padj05")),
             paste0("ρ = ", metric(val, "spearman_lfc_all")), metric(val, "signature_auc"),
             paste0(round(metric(val, "signature_pairs_tumor_gt_normal") * metric(val, "complete_pairs")), " / ",
                    metric(val, "complete_pairs")),
             paste0("r = ", metric(val, "hallmark_nes_pearson")),
             paste0(metric(val, "hallmark_replicated"), " / ", nrow(h_sig))))
kable(vt, caption = "Replication of TCGA findings in GSE104131")
```

Direction agreement is far beyond chance (binomial p < 10^-16^). Many TCGA DEGs do not reach significance in GEO because 13 pairs give much less power, but they point the same way. The cohort is restricted to high-grade tumors, which makes this a stricter test than a grade-matched replication.

```{r fig-val, fig.cap = "Left: gene-level fold changes. Right: TCGA signature score in GEO samples.", fig.show = "hold", out.width = "48%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c(f("results/validation/lfc_concordance.png"),
                          f("results/validation/tcga_signature_score.png")))
```

```{r fig-nes, fig.cap = "Hallmark NES in TCGA vs GSE104131."}
img("results/validation/hallmark_nes_concordance.png", "65%")
```

# Exploratory ancestry analysis

TCGA-PRAD has few patients of African ancestry. Only `r n_black_pairs` of the `r n_pairs` paired patients self-report as Black or African American, which is too few for a paired subgroup analysis. Two complementary analyses were therefore run. Both rely on **self-reported race or ethnicity, which is not genetic ancestry**.

## Does the tumor effect differ by ancestry? (GSE104131)

Pairs were nested within ancestry (7 AA, 6 EA). At gene level, `r metric(anc, "geo_interaction_genes")` genes had an ancestry-specific tumor effect. At pathway level, each patient was treated as one observation. For each pair and Hallmark set, the score is the mean tumor-minus-normal change of the set's genes, compared between AA and EA with an exact Wilcoxon test. **No set differed** (smallest raw p = `r signif(min(geo_ph$p_wilcox), 2)`).

An earlier version ranked genes by the interaction statistic and ran pre-ranked GSEA. That flagged 41 of 50 sets, with p-values below 10^-20^. Pre-ranked GSEA treats genes as independent. With 13 patients, a few atypical pairs shift thousands of correlated genes together, so those p-values were far too small. The patient-level test replaces it. This cohort does not support or rule out ancestry-specific tumor biology. It is simply underpowered.

```{r fig-geo-anc, fig.cap = "Per-pair Hallmark tumor effects for the eight lowest-p sets."}
img("results/ancestry/geo_ancestry_hallmark_pairlevel.png", "95%")
```

## Tumors from Black vs White patients (TCGA)

`r metric(anc, "tcga_tumors_black")` tumors from Black and `r metric(anc, "tcga_tumors_white")` from White patients were compared, adjusting for Gleason group and age. Grade differs markedly between the groups: `r hg("Black")` vs `r hg("White")` Gleason 8–10.

**A mapping artifact.** Before filtering, the strongest "race" genes were mitochondrial pseudogenes (`r nrow(mt)` significant, `r sum(mt$log2FC > 0)` higher in Black patients). The likely cause is that African mitochondrial haplogroups differ from the European reference mitochondrial genome. Some mitochondrial reads then align to nuclear copies of mitochondrial DNA instead. These were removed, and DEG reporting was restricted to protein-coding and lncRNA genes.

```{r fig-race, fig.cap = "Hallmark GSEA, Black vs White tumors.", out.width = "80%"}
img("results/ancestry/tcga_race_hallmark.png", "80%")
```

```{r race-ifn}
ifn <- site_h[grepl("INTERFERON|ALLOGRAFT|TNFA|INFLAMMATORY", pathway)][order(-NES_site)]
kable(ifn[, .(Pathway = short(pathway), `NES (all sites)` = round(NES_main, 2), `padj` = signif(padj_main, 2),
              `NES (site-matched)` = round(NES_site, 2), `padj ` = signif(padj_site, 2))],
      caption = "Immune and interferon sets, main model vs site-matched model")
```

Interferon-α, interferon-γ and allograft-rejection sets are higher in tumors from Black patients. This agrees with earlier reports of an interferon and immune-inflammation signature in African-American prostate tumors (Wallace et al. 2008; Awasthi et al. 2021). Because Black patients come mostly from a few tissue source sites, race and site are confounded. Restricting to sites with ≥ 3 Black and ≥ 3 White patients (`r metric(anc, "site_matched_black")` vs `r metric(anc, "site_matched_white")`) and adding site to the model leaves the interferon result intact. TNFα/NF-κB and inflammatory-response sets also become significant. The stromal and metabolic sets lower in Black patients are less stable: overall NES correlation between the two models is r = `r metric(anc, "site_matched_nes_r")`.

```{r fig-site, fig.cap = "Robustness of race-associated Hallmark NES to tissue source site."}
img("results/ancestry/tcga_race_site_matched_nes.png", "60%")
```

Several top individual genes (e.g. TDO2, RBM44, MAEL, TRIM31) show large, consistent shifts. Large single-gene differences between population groups can come from inherited variants rather than tumor biology; this is tested with genetic ancestry in the next section.

# Genetic ancestry

Self-reported race is a social category, not a measure of genetic ancestry. Per-patient ancestry proportions estimated from germline genotypes by the TCGA Ancestry & Molecular Correlates group (Carrot-Zhang et al. 2020; source file: `r gv("ancestry_source")`) were used instead. **AFR** below is the fraction of a patient's genome estimated to be of African ancestry (0–1).

```{r tab-ga-race}
kable(ga_sh[, .(n = .N, `Median AFR` = round(median(afr), 2), `Range` = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(afr), max(afr)),
               `AFR ≥ 0.5` = sum(afr >= 0.5)), by = .(`Self-reported race` = race)],
      caption = "Genetic African-ancestry fraction by self-reported race (TCGA-PRAD primary tumors)")
```

```{r fig-ga-race, fig.cap = "Self-reported race vs genetic African-ancestry fraction."}
img("results/genetic_ancestry/race_vs_genetic_ancestry.png", "60%")
```

Self-identified Black patients have a median AFR of `r gv("black_median_afr")` (minimum `r gv("black_min_afr")`), the admixed range typical of African Americans. The highest AFR among self-identified White patients is `r gv("white_max_afr")`. `r if (gv("other_unknown_afr_ge_0.5") > 0) paste0(gv("other_unknown_afr_ge_0.5"), " patient(s) with missing or other self-reported race have AFR ≥ 0.5, so genetic data also recover ancestry information that self-report lacks.") else ""`

## Expression and African-ancestry fraction

Tumors from patients of two-way African/European ancestry (`r gv("two_way_tumors")` tumors, `r gv("two_way_afr_ge_0.5")` with AFR ≥ 0.5) were modelled as `~ Gleason group + age + AFR`. Treating ancestry as a continuous dose uses the variation within admixed patients, rather than a two-group label. `r gv("afr_genes_fdr05")` protein-coding or lncRNA genes are associated with AFR at FDR < 0.05, and `r gv("afr_hallmark_fdr05")` Hallmark sets are enriched.

```{r fig-ga-nes, fig.cap = "Hallmark NES by self-reported race (M6) vs by genetic AFR fraction."}
img("results/genetic_ancestry/afr_vs_race_nes.png", "65%")
```

Pathway results correlate at r = `r gv("nes_r_afr_vs_race")` between the two definitions. In the gene-set analysis, interferon-γ response has NES = `r round(ifng_afr$NES_afr, 2)` per unit AFR (adjusted p = `r signif(ifng_afr$padj_afr, 2)`), so the interferon association `r if (ifn_afr_sig) "is reproduced with genetic ancestry" else "is not reproduced with genetic ancestry at FDR < 0.05"`.

Gene-set tests rank genes and treat them as independent, so co-regulated genes such as an interferon programme can make the p-value look more certain than the data allow. The patient-level test below scores each tumor once and regresses that score on AFR. There, the shift is `r sprintf("%+.2f", ifn_pt_b)` SD from AFR 0 to 1 (p = `r signif(ifn_pt_p, 2)`), `r if (ifn_pt_sig) "which supports a real but modest difference" else "the same direction but not statistically distinguishable from no difference"`. The patient-level estimate is the more conservative reading.

```{r tab-ga-ifn}
kable(ga_ifn[, .(Model = model, `Change in IFN-γ score (SD) from AFR 0 to 1` = round(beta_sd_per_full_AFR, 2), p = signif(p, 2))],
      caption = "Interferon-γ score vs African-ancestry fraction")
```

The second row adds MCP-counter T-cell and B-lineage scores, testing again whether the association runs through immune-cell content (Section on tissue composition). The third row uses variation in AFR among self-identified Black patients with AFR ≥ 0.5 only, which is less exposed to differences between collection sites.

## Are the top race-associated genes inherited signals?

For the `r nrow(ga_gt)` genes most strongly associated with self-reported race (M6), expression was regressed on AFR in three settings. A gene is flagged as a likely **germline** signal if it tracks AFR across all tumors (FDR < 0.05, same direction as the race effect) **and** also tracks AFR either within self-identified Black patients with AFR ≥ 0.5 or in matched normal tissue (p < 0.05, same direction). The two self-identified Black patients with near-zero African ancestry are left out of the within-group test, where they would otherwise dominate the fit. The normal-tissue test rests on only `r gv("normals_afr_ge_0.5")` normal samples with AFR ≥ 0.5, so it has little power. Tracking ancestry in normal tissue, or as a dose-response within one self-reported group, is hard to explain by tumor biology or by social factors linked to the race label.

```{r tab-germline}
kable(ga_gt[order(p_all_tumors)][1:min(15, .N), .(Gene = gene, `Race log2FC` = round(race_log2FC, 2),
        `β tumors` = round(beta_all_tumors, 2), `padj tumors` = signif(padj_all_tumors, 2),
        `β within Black` = round(beta_within_black, 2), `p within Black` = signif(p_within_black, 2),
        `β normals` = round(beta_normals, 2), `p normals` = signif(p_normals, 2), Germline = likely_germline)],
      caption = "Top race-associated genes vs genetic AFR fraction (β = change in log2 TPM from AFR 0 to 1)")
```

```{r fig-germline, fig.cap = "Expression vs African-ancestry fraction for the six genes most associated with AFR, in tumors (top) and matched normals (bottom)."}
img("results/genetic_ancestry/germline_gene_scatter.png", "100%")
```

`r if (nrow(germ)) paste0(nrow(germ), " gene(s) meet the germline criteria: ", paste(germ$gene, collapse = ", "), ". These are better explained by common inherited variants whose frequency differs between African and European populations (for example expression QTLs or copy-number polymorphisms) than by tumor biology, and should not be read as tumor biomarkers of race.") else "No gene meets the germline criteria; with few Black patients and few normal samples from them, the within-group and normal-tissue tests have limited power, so this is not evidence against a germline origin."` Confirming a specific variant would need the germline genotypes, which are controlled-access.

# Tissue composition

Bulk RNA-seq measures a mixture of tumor cells, stroma and immune cells. Composition was estimated for every sample with three signature-based methods: **ESTIMATE** stromal and immune scores (Yoshihara et al. 2013), **MCP-counter** abundance scores for eight immune and two stromal populations (Becht et al. 2016), and marker scores for smooth muscle (ACTG2, DES, CNN1, MYH11, ACTA2, TAGLN) and basal epithelium (KRT5, KRT15, TP63). These are relative scores, not absolute cell fractions.

## Tumor vs matched normal

```{r tab-paired-comp}
key <- c("estimate_stromal", "estimate_immune", "mcp_Fibroblasts", "smooth_muscle", "basal_epithelium",
         "mcp_Endothelial_cells", "mcp_T_cells")
kable(dc_pt[score %in% key][order(p), .(Score = score, `Median normal` = round(median_normal, 2),
        `Median tumor` = round(median_tumor, 2), `Tumor higher (pairs)` = paste0(tumor_higher_pairs, " / ", pairs),
        `Adjusted p` = signif(padj, 2))],
      caption = "Composition in paired samples (Wilcoxon signed-rank, BH-adjusted)")
```

```{r fig-paired-comp, fig.cap = "Composition scores in each patient's tumor and normal sample."}
img("results/deconv/paired_composition.png", "95%")
```

## Which pathway changes reflect composition?

The paired model was refitted twice:

1. `~ patient + stromal + immune + condition`, using ESTIMATE scores.
2. The same, plus the smooth-muscle and basal-epithelium scores.

The second model is needed because ESTIMATE's stromal signature is built from fibroblast and extracellular-matrix genes, while prostate stroma is mostly smooth muscle. Tumor status correlates with the ESTIMATE stromal score at only r = `r mval(dcs, "cor_tumor_stromal")`, but with the smooth-muscle score at r = `r mval(dcs, "cor_tumor_smooth_muscle")` and the basal score at r = `r mval(dcs, "cor_tumor_basal")`. Each adjustment removes the part of a change explained by differing composition between a patient's two samples.

```{r adj-lists}
sens_est  <- dc_ah[class == "composition-sensitive"][order(-NES_main)]
sens_full <- dc_ah[class != "composition-sensitive" & class_full == "composition-sensitive"][order(-NES_main)]
emerg     <- dc_ah[class_full == "emerges after adjustment" | class == "emerges after adjustment"][order(-NES_main)]
```

- **Robust under both adjustments (`r nrow(core)`):** `r if (nrow(core)) paste(short(core$pathway), collapse = ", ") else "none"`.
- **Lost after ESTIMATE adjustment (`r nrow(sens_est)`):** `r if (nrow(sens_est)) paste(short(sens_est$pathway), collapse = ", ") else "none"`. These mostly reflect immune and fibroblast content.
- **Lost only after adding smooth muscle and basal scores (`r nrow(sens_full)`):** `r if (nrow(sens_full)) paste(short(sens_full$pathway), collapse = ", ") else "none"`. These mostly reflect loss of fibromuscular stroma and basal cells.
- **Significant only after adjustment (`r nrow(emerg)`):** `r if (nrow(emerg)) paste(short(emerg$pathway), collapse = ", ") else "none"`.

The robust sets are the strongest candidates for changes within tumor cells. The smooth-muscle score shares genes with the Hallmark myogenesis set, so myogenesis weakening under the second model is partly circular rather than evidence by itself.

```{r fig-adj, fig.cap = "Hallmark NES before and after composition adjustment, for both adjusted models."}
img("results/deconv/adjusted_paired_hallmark.png", "100%")
```

## Composition and the race comparison

```{r tab-race-comp}
kable(dc_rc[order(p)][1:min(8, .N), .(Score = score, `Difference (SD, Black − White)` = round(diff_sd_black_vs_white, 2),
        `Adjusted p` = signif(padj, 2))],
      caption = "Composition of Black vs White patients' tumors (linear model with Gleason group and age)")
```

```{r fig-race-comp, fig.cap = "Tumor composition by self-reported race."}
img("results/deconv/race_composition.png", "95%")
```

Immune content is modestly higher in Black patients' tumors (ESTIMATE immune score `r sprintf("%+.2f", mval(dcs, "race_immune_diff_sd"))` SD, adjusted p = `r mval(dcs, "race_immune_padj")`). To ask whether this explains the interferon difference, the race model was adjusted in two ways:

- **ESTIMATE stromal and immune scores.** `r mval(dcs, "estimate_immune_ifn_overlap_genes")` genes of the ESTIMATE immune signature are also in the Hallmark interferon sets, so this adjustment can remove interferon signal itself.
- **MCP-counter T-cell, B-lineage and fibroblast scores**, which are built from lineage marker genes.

```{r tab-ifn}
ifn_tab <- dc_ra[grepl("INTERFERON|ALLOGRAFT", pathway)]
kable(ifn_tab[, .(Pathway = short(pathway), `NES main` = round(NES_main, 2), `padj main` = signif(padj_main, 2),
                  `NES ESTIMATE-adj` = round(NES_est, 2), `padj ESTIMATE` = signif(padj_est, 2),
                  `NES MCP-adj` = round(NES_mcp, 2), `padj MCP` = signif(padj_mcp, 2))],
      caption = "Interferon and allograft-rejection sets, Black vs White tumors, under each adjustment")
```

The interferon difference `r ifn_text`. Across all 50 Hallmark sets, the median NES shifts by `r sprintf("%+.2f", mval(dcs, "race_nes_median_shift_estimate"))` after the ESTIMATE adjustment and `r sprintf("%+.2f", mval(dcs, "race_nes_median_shift_mcp"))` after the MCP-counter adjustment. A large uniform shift means the adjustment moves almost every pathway at once, a sign of over-adjustment rather than pathway-specific biology. Bulk RNA-seq cannot fully separate "more immune cells" from "more interferon activity per cell"; spatial or single-cell data would be needed to settle it.

# Association with progression

**Outcome.** Progression-free interval (PFI) from the TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource (Liu et al. 2018), the endpoint recommended for TCGA-PRAD because deaths are few. **Samples.** One primary tumor per patient: `r mval(svs, "tumors_with_pfi")` tumors with `r mval(svs, "pfi_events")` progression events and median follow-up `r mval(svs, "median_followup_months")` months. **Models.** Cox proportional hazards per standard deviation of each score, univariable and adjusted for Gleason group, pathological T stage and age (`r mval(svs, "cox_complete_cases")` complete cases, `r mval(svs, "cox_events")` events). The clinical-only model has C-index `r mval(svs, "c_index_clinical")`.

```{r tab-cox}
kable(cox_adj[, .(Score = score, `HR per SD` = round(HR_per_SD, 2),
                  `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", lower95, upper95), `Adjusted p` = signif(padj, 2),
                  `C-index` = round(c_index, 3), `Gain vs clinical` = sprintf("%+.3f", c_gain_vs_clinical),
                  `PH test p` = signif(ph_global_p, 2))],
      caption = "Cox models adjusted for Gleason group, T stage and age (BH across scores)")
```

```{r fig-forest, fig.cap = "Adjusted hazard ratios per SD with 95% confidence intervals."}
img("results/survival/forest_plot.png", "75%")
```

```{r fig-km, fig.cap = "Kaplan–Meier curves, median split (unadjusted)."}
img("results/survival/km_plots.png", "100%")
```

`r if (n_cox_sig == 0) paste0("**No score was independently associated with progression.** After adjusting for Gleason group, T stage and age, hazard ratios ranged from ", round(min(cox_adj$HR_per_SD), 2), " to ", round(max(cox_adj$HR_per_SD), 2), " per SD, and the largest C-index gain over the clinical model was ", sprintf("%+.3f", best_gain$c_gain_vs_clinical), " (", best_gain$score, ").") else paste0("**", n_cox_sig, " score(s) remained associated with progression after adjustment:** ", hr_txt(cox_adj[padj < 0.05]), ".")` `r if (nrow(uni_sig)) paste0("Before adjustment, ", paste0(uni_sig$score, " (HR ", round(uni_sig$HR_per_SD, 2), ", adjusted p = ", signif(uni_sig$padj, 2), ")", collapse = "; "), " predicted faster progression. High-grade tumors proliferate more, so this prognostic signal is largely carried by Gleason grade.") else ""` Median-split curves are shown for illustration only; the Cox models are the formal test. Only `r mval(svs, "events_black")` of `r mval(svs, "n_black")` Black patients had a progression event, too few to test whether any association differs by race.

# Limitations

- **Bulk tissue.** Tumor-vs-normal differences mix changes in cell state with changes in cell-type composition, especially stromal loss. ESTIMATE and MCP-counter give relative signature scores, not true cell fractions, and adjusting for them can also remove real biology when composition and condition are intertwined.
- **Progression.** PFI in prostate cancer mostly reflects new tumor events after surgery, follow-up is short, and the scores were not tested in an independent outcome cohort.
- **Purity.** Published purity estimates exist for only some samples. All pairs were kept, and results were robust to excluding the borderline ones.
- **Validation cohort.** GSE104131 is small (13 pairs) and high-grade only, with counts from a different pipeline and annotation (Entrez IDs mapped to symbols).
- **Ancestry.** Self-reported race is not genetic ancestry; genetic ancestry proportions were used as a check (Section on genetic ancestry), but African-ancestry samples remain few. Race and ancestry are confounded with collection site and grade in TCGA. Tumor-only comparisons cannot show tumor-vs-normal differences. All ancestry results are exploratory.
- **Multiple testing.** FDR is controlled within each analysis, not across the whole project.
